Slide 4: What is NMR?Nuclear Magnetic ResonanceA magnet, a glass of water, and a radio wave source and detector.Water Magnetism: Is water magnetic? Yes, weakly (Diamagnetism).Nuclear Magnetism:$O^{16}$ (even protons/neutrons) $\rightarrow$ No magnetic moment.$H^1$ (proton, spin 1/2) $\rightarrow$ Magnetic Moment.Slide 6: Spins and Nuclear MagnetismNet Alignment:The macroscopic magnetization vector 1$\vec{M}$ is the vector sum of individual moments 2$\vec{m}$:3$$ \vec{M} = \sum \vec{m} $$We manipulate and observe this macroscopic ensemble.

```{r, echo=FALSE}

include_graphics(file.path(img_dir, "slide_6.png"))
```
Slide 10: Magnetic Energy StatesTwo ways of saying the same thing:The field torques the needle (magnetization) into alignment.Alignment along North is the lowest energy state.$$ E = - \vec{\mu} \cdot \vec{B} = - \cos \theta $$Quantum Mechanics: Only two observable energy states ("up" and "down").$$ \Delta E = h\nu $$Slide 11: Thermal EquilibriumThermal energy jostles some spins into the high-energy state.The net alignment grows as $\Delta E$ gets bigger (higher field) or Temperature gets cold.Boltzmann Distribution:$$ \frac{N_{\uparrow} - N_{\downarrow}}{N_{TOT}} \approx 1 - e^{-\Delta E/kT} \approx 10^{-4} $$Slide 12: Gyroscopic MotionProtons have spin (angular momentum) and a magnetic moment.Result: Precession around the main field $B_0$.The Larmor Equation:(The only equation you need to know)$$ \nu_0 = \gamma B_0 $$$\gamma/2\pi \approx 42.58 \text{ MHz/T}$At 3 Tesla: $\nu_0 \approx 127 \text{ MHz}$Slide 24: Detecting the SignalFaraday's Law (Generator Effect):A moving bar magnet induces a voltage in a coil of wire.4Flux: $\Phi = n B_{spins} A$Induced Voltage:$$ V(t) = -\frac{d\Phi}{dt} $$The RF coil design is the #1 determinant of the system SNR.Slide 25: Signal StrengthThe signal is proportional to the rate of change of the flux.$$ \Phi(t) \propto M_0 \cos(\omega t) $$$$ V(t) \propto -M_0 \omega \sin(\omega t) $$Since $M_0 \propto B_0$ and $\omega \propto B_0$:$$ \text{Signal } V(t) \propto B_0^2 $$Slide 27: Three Steps in MRIEquilibrium: Magnetization points along $z$ ($B_0$).RF Excitation: Tip magnetization away from equilibrium.Precession: Induces signal.Signal phase/decay timescale: $T_2, T_2^*$.Return to equilibrium timescale: $T_1$.Slide 33: Proton Density ContrastEncode image immediately after excitation (Short TE, Long TR).Tissue with more protons per cc gives more signal (brighter).No chance to dephase (minimized $T_2$ effects).Magnetization fully relaxed (minimized $T_1$ effects).The most boring contrast...

# Slide 34: T2* Dephasing Contrast

Wait a time (TE) before measuring.Shorter $T_2^*$ spins have dephased.Iron and myelin rich tissues dephase faster (appear dark).We choose TE to maximize the intensity difference.$$ S(t) = S_0 e^{-t/T_2^*} $$

# Slide 38: Computational Graphic - T2* Decay

(Regenerated using Python via Reticulate)

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define Time to Encode (TE) range
t = np.linspace(0, 150, 300)

# Approximate T2* values (ms)
T2s_tissue1 = 60.0  # e.g. Grey Matter
T2s_tissue2 = 200.0 # e.g. CSF/Water

# Decay Equation
S1 = np.exp(-t / T2s_tissue1)
S2 = np.exp(-t / T2s_tissue2)

plt.figure(figsize=(7, 4))
plt.plot(t, S2, 'g--', label=r'Tissue 1 ($T_2^*=200$)', linewidth=2)
plt.plot(t, S1, 'b-', label=r'Tissue 2 ($T_2^*=60$)', linewidth=2)

# Arrow for max contrast
plt.annotate('Max Contrast', xy=(40, 0.5), xytext=(60, 0.7),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', shrink=0.05))

plt.title(r'Transverse Magnetization Decay ($T_2^*$ Contrast)')
plt.xlabel('Time to Encode (TE) [ms]')
plt.ylabel('Signal ($M_{xy}$)')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Slide 45: Gradient vs. Spin Echo

Gradient Echo:Accelerates dephasing with a gradient ($G_x$), then reverses it.Sensitive to static field inhomogeneities ($T_2^*$).Spin Echo (The Parlor Trick):Uses a $180^\circ$ RF pulse to re-phase spins.Cancels out static field inhomogeneities.Measures "true" $T_2$ (random molecular interactions).

# Slide 50: T1 Contrast

Saturation Recovery:To control $T_1$ recovery, vary the Time to Repetition (TR).$$ M_z(TR) = M_0 (1 - e^{-TR/T_1}) $$White Matter (Short $T_1$): Recovers fast $\rightarrow$ Bright.Grey Matter (Long $T_1$): Recovers slow $\rightarrow$ Dark.

# Slide 52: Computational Graphic - T1 Recovery

(Regenerated using Python via Reticulate)

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

TR = np.linspace(0, 3000, 300)

# Approximate T1 values at 3T (ms)
T1_WM = 600.0    # White Matter
T1_GM = 1000.0   # Grey Matter
T1_CSF = 3000.0  # CSF

# Saturation Recovery Equation
S_WM = 1 - np.exp(-TR / T1_WM)
S_GM = 1 - np.exp(-TR / T1_GM)
S_CSF = 1 - np.exp(-TR / T1_CSF)

plt.figure(figsize=(7, 4))
plt.plot(TR, S_WM, 'r--', label='White Matter (T1=600)')
plt.plot(TR, S_GM, 'b-', label='Grey Matter (T1=1000)')
plt.plot(TR, S_CSF, 'y:', label='CSF (T1=3000)')

plt.axvline(x=600, color='k', linestyle=':', label='Optimal Contrast TR')
plt.title('T1 Weighting (Saturation Recovery)')
plt.xlabel('Repetition Time (TR) [ms]')
plt.ylabel('Signal ($M_z$)')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Slide 57: BOLD Contrast Basics

Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent (BOLD)Hemodynamic Changes:Direct Flow effects.Blood oxygenation effects.Magnetic Properties:Oxygenated Hemoglobin: Diamagnetic (non-magnetic).De-oxygenated Hemoglobin: Paramagnetic (magnetic).

# Slide 61: The BOLD Mechanism

Biologist's Analysis (Correct):Activation: Tissue sucks only a little more $O_2$.Response: Blood flow & volume go up massively.Result: Oxygenated blood floods the voxel.Physics: Deoxy-Hb concentration decreases.MRI: Less magnetic stuff $\rightarrow$ Less dephasing $\rightarrow$ Signal Goes UP.

# Slide 66: Computational Graphic - BOLD Optimization

We want to maximize Contrast to Noise Ratio (CNR).$$ CNR \propto TE \cdot e^{-TE/T_2^*} $$Differentiation shows maximum contrast occurs when TE = T2*.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

TE = np.linspace(0, 200, 200)
T2_star = 50.0 # Typical T2* for brain at 3T

# BOLD contrast model
CNR = TE * np.exp(-TE / T2_star)

plt.figure(figsize=(7, 4))
plt.plot(TE, CNR, 'g-', linewidth=2)
plt.axvline(x=T2_star, color='r', linestyle='--', label='Optimum TE = T2*')

plt.title('BOLD Sensitivity Optimization')
plt.xlabel('Echo Time (TE) [ms]')
plt.ylabel('Contrast to Noise Ratio (CNR)')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Slide 70: Vessel Size Specificity

Paramagnetic agent in blood:Big Vessel (Venule): Field is constant on length scale of diffusion.Capillaries: Water diffuses through field gradients (dynamic averaging).Conclusion: Spin Echo BOLD is more specific to capillaries, while Gradient Echo BOLD sees all vessels.
